stemMd: The function $P(t) = 8{,}000(0.81)^t$ models the number of fish in a lake $t$ years after a survey began. Which statement best describes how the modeled number of fish changes every $6$ months?
explanationMd:
The model gives the yearly factor, $0.81$. Six months is half a year, so the factor for $6$ months is the number that, applied **twice**, gives $0.81$. That is a square root, not half:

$$\sqrt{0.81} = 0.9 \qquad\text{because}\qquad 0.9 \times 0.9 = 0.81$$

Rewriting the model makes this visible:

$$P(t) = 8{,}000(0.81)^t = 8{,}000\left(0.9^2\right)^t = 8{,}000(0.9)^{2t}$$

Here $2t$ counts half-year periods, and each half-year multiplies the population by $0.9$. Multiplying by $0.9$ is a decrease of $1 - 0.9 = 0.10$, or $10\%$.

Check with numbers: starting from $8{,}000$, after $6$ months $8{,}000 \times 0.9 = 7{,}200$, and after another $6$ months $7{,}200 \times 0.9 = 6{,}480$. The model gives $P(1) = 8{,}000 \times 0.81 = 6{,}480$ directly, so the half-year factor is right.

Note that two $10\%$ decreases make a $19\%$ decrease over the year, not $20\%$: percent changes compound rather than add, which is why halving the yearly $19\%$ to $9.5\%$ does not work.

distractorRationale.c: This halves the yearly decrease of $19\%$. Percent decreases compound: two decreases of $9.5\%$ multiply the population by $0.905^2 \approx 0.819$, not $0.81$.
distractorRationale.b: This is the decrease over a full year, since $1 - 0.81 = 0.19$. Over $6$ months the factor is $\sqrt{0.81} = 0.9$, a $10\%$ decrease.
distractorRationale.a: This halves the factor, $0.81 \div 2 = 0.405$, and reads $1 - 0.405$ as the decrease. The half-year factor is the square root of $0.81$, not half of it.

accessibilityText: The function P of t equals 8,000 times 0.81 to the power t models the number of fish in a lake t years after a survey began. Which statement best describes how the number of fish changes every 6 months? The choices are: it decreases by 10 percent every 6 months; it decreases by 9.5 percent every 6 months; it decreases by 19 percent every 6 months; it decreases by 59.5 percent every 6 months.

provenance.notes: Original item. Converts a yearly exponential decay factor to a half-year factor, where the factor is the square root of 0.81 rather than half of the yearly rate.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Per half-year factor is 0.81^(1/2) = 0.9, a 10% decrease every 6 months. 19% is the annual decrease, 9.5% halves the annual rate linearly, 59.5% is nonsensical. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave8-sat-math-run1) reached the same answer: Half-year factor = 0.81^(1/2) = 0.9, a 10% decrease every 6 months. 19% is the annual decrease; 9.5% halves the annual rate linearly; 59.5% has no valid derivation.]
